sections.content:
Population change in Tower Hamlets in 2032

The population in Tower Hamlets is projected to increase from 323,854 people in 2022 to 389,845 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 87,576 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Tower Hamlets
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Tower Hamlets, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 34,123, with 47,327 births and 13,204 deaths in Tower Hamlets between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Tower Hamlets by 10.5%, compared with an increase of 6.0% in London and an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 59,612, with 355,582 people moving to the area and 415,194 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Tower Hamlets by 18.4%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to increase the population by 3,311, with 10,742 people moving to the area and 7,432 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Tower Hamlets by 1.0%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 87,576, with 165,687 people moving to the area and 78,111 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Tower Hamlets by 27.0%, compared with an increase of 14.7% in London and an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.subtitle: Projected population age structure by single year of age and sex for Tower Hamlets, 2022 to 2047
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Age profile in Tower Hamlets in 2032

The median age in Tower Hamlets is projected to rise from 30 years in 2022 to 31 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 6% of the population in Tower Hamlets are projected to be aged 65 years or over, around the same as in 2022.

sections.title: The 10 to 19 age group are set to see the largest change in Tower Hamlets between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Tower Hamlets is projected to stay the same, at around 78%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 67 to 70 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Tower Hamlets?

In 2032, 19% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 21% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Tower Hamlets between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 6%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
